  26|                           may, after the receipt of an appropriate court order or consent of the property owner, enter the property
  27|                           and physically remove the installation at the owner's expense. As a condition of development plan re-
  28|                           view, a property owner shall agree to allow the Town entry to remove an abandoned or decommis-
  29|                          sioned installation. The cost for the removal will be charged to the property owner in accordance with
  30|                          the provisions of MGL c. 139, § 3A as a tax lien on the property.
  31|                          (12) Financial surety. Proponents of large-scale solar photovoltaic projects shall provide a form of
  32|                           surety, either through an escrow account, bond or otherwise, to cover the cost of removal in the event
  33|                           the Town must remove the installation and remediate the landscape, in an amount and form deter-
  34|                          mined to be reasonable by the development plan review authority, but in no event to exceed more than
  35|                           125% of the cost of removal and compliance with the additional requirements set forth herein, as de-
  36|                          termined by the project proponent. Such surety will not be required for municipally or state-owned
  37|                          facilities. The project owner/operator shall submit a fully inclusive estimate of the costs associated
  38|                          with removal, prepared by a qualified engineer. The amount shall include a mechanism for calculating
  39|                          increased removal cost due to inflation.
  40|                           E. Inclusionary uses and conflicts.
  41|                          (1) Small accessory or ornamental solar products which do not generate electricity for use in a dwell-
  42|                          ing or structure are exempt from the provisions in this bylaw. 8 (2) In the event that any part of this
  43|                          section conflicts with other requirements of the Zoning Bylaw, the requirements of this section shall
  44|                          apply.
  45|                           § 250-4.16 14 Registered marijuana dispensaries.
  46|                          [Added 5-3-2014 ATM by Art. 27]
  47|                           A. Purpose: to provide for the placement of registered marijuana dispensaries (RMDs), in accordance
  48|                          with the Humanitarian Medical Use of Marijuana Act, MGL c. 94C, App. 1-1 - Chapter 369 of the
  49|                          Acts of 2012, in locations suitable for lawful medical marijuana facilities and to minimize adverse im-
  50|                          pact of RMDs on adjacent properties, residential neighborhoods, historic districts, schools, play-
  51|                          grounds and other locations where minors congregate by regulating the siting, design, placement, secu-
  52|                          rity and removal of RMDs.
  53|                                                                                              215

===PAGE 216=== (ocr, 53 lines)
   1|                        B. Applicability.
   2|                        (1) All RMDs shall comply with the regulations promulgated by the Massachusetts Department of Pub-
   3|                        lic Health (DPH), 105 CMR 725.000, Implementation of an Act for the Humanitarian Medical Use of
   4|                         Marijuana, effective May 24, 2013, and any subsequent amendments thereto.
   5|                        (2) The Town reserves the right to require compliance with provisions in the DPH regulations for which
   6|                        the state granted waivers and/or exemptions to the RMD applicant based on the provisions of § 250-
   7|                        8.3C (as to special permits) and § 250-8.4 (as to development plan review).
   8|                        C. Definition. As used in this section, the following terms shall have the meanings indicated:
   9|                        REGISTERED MARIJUANA DISPENSARY
  10|                         Also known as a "medical marijuana treatment center," means a not-for-profit entity registered under
  11|                        105 CMR 725.000 that acquires, cultivates, possesses, processes (including development of related
  12|                         products such as edible marijuana-infused products, tinctures, aerosols, oils, or ointments), transfers,
  13|                         transports, sells, distributes, dispenses, or administers marijuana, products containing marijuana, related
  14|                         supplies, or educational materials to registered qualifying patients or their personal caregivers. Unless
  15|                        otherwise specified, "RMD" refers to the site(s) of dispensing, cultivation, and preparation of marijua-
  16|                        na.
  17|                        D. Location.
  18|                        (1) RMDs that include retail, processing and cultivation are allowed in Commercial Districts (C) by
  19|                        special permit.
  20|                        (2) Cultivation and/or agricultural processing: Allowed in all Residential Districts by Special Permit but
  21|                        Cultivation and/or agricultural processing are allowed in all districts by right if the applicant is eligible
  22|                        quire a special permit.
  23|                        (3) RMD facilities that cultivate and process, but do not do retail of marijuana, are allowed in Office
  24|                        Park and Industrial Districts (OP/I) by special permit.
  25|                        (4) All cultivation must be conducted within a building which must be located at least five hundred
  26|                        (500) feet from any residential property line.
  27|                        E. Procedure for submittal. 9 (1) The Planning Board shall be the special permit granting authority
  28|                        (SPGA) for a RMD special permit per MGL c. 40A, § 9. Siting shall be by special permit and develop-
  29|                        ment plan review per § 250-8.4 of the Lunenburg Protective Bylaw.
  30|                        (2) Criteria. In granting any special permit, the Planning Board shall assure that the proposed use:
  31|                        (a) Will not be injurious or dangerous to the public health or unduly hazardous because of traffic con-
  32|                         gestion, danger or fire or explosion or other reasons.
  33|                        (b) Will not have a material adverse effect on the value of land and buildings in the neighborhood or on
  34|                        the amenities of the neighborhood.
  35|                        (c) Will be operated with reasonable regard for order and sightliness, if an open use.
  36|                        (d) Will not produce noise, vibration, smoke, dust, odor, heat or glare observable at the lot lines in
  37|                        amounts clearly detrimental to the normal use of adjacent property.
  38|                        (3) It is recommended that a concept plan showing the proposed use shall be submitted to the Planning
  39|                         Board for review and discussion prior to the filing for development plan review.
  40|                        (4) The provisions of § 250-8.3C (as to special permits) and § 250-8.4 (as to development plan re-
  41|                        view) shall apply.
  42|                        (5) Filing under §§ 250-8.3C and 250-8.4 may be simultaneous.
  43|                        (6) A special permit granted under this section shall have a term limited to the duration of the appli-
  44|                              cant's ownership of the premises as a RMD. A special permit may be transferred only with the ap-
  45|                              proval of the special permit granting authority in the form of an amendment to the special permit
  46|                               with all information required in this section.
  47|                        F. Conditional standards.
  48|                        (1) Distance. All proposed RMDs shall be sited accordingly as stated in Massachusetts Department of
  49|                        Public Health (DPH) 105 CMR 725.110(A)(14), which states a RMD shall not be sited within a radius
  50|                         of 500 feet of a school, day-care center, or any facility in which children commonly congregate. The
  51|                         five-hundred-foot distance under this section is measured in a straight line from the nearest point of the
  52|                        proposed RMD.
  53|                                                                                              216

===PAGE 217=== (ocr, 53 lines)
   1|                          (2) Setbacks and buffer strips. Cultivation facilities located outside of Retail Commercial (RC), Com-
   2|                          mercial (C), or Office Park and Industrial Districts (OP/I) shall be surrounded by a buffer strip which
   3|                          shall be five hundred (500)200 feet in depth unless the applicant can demonstrate, and the Planning
   4|                          Board finds, that adequate buffering can be provided in a narrower buffer strip. In all other districts,
   5|                          existing setbacks will apply.
   6|                          (3) Design standards. In addition to requirements contained elsewhere in this bylaw, § 250-4.6E, De-
   7|                          sign standards, shall be applicable to a RMD. The applicant shall meet all requirements of the Commer-
   8|                          cial District (C) or DPH guidelines, whichever is more restrictive.
   9|                         (4) Waivers. The Planning Board may waive any of the non-dimensional conditional standards within
  10|                          this section, provided that such waiver will not derogate from the intent established herein.
  11|                          G. Security.
  12|                          (1) All security measures shall be approved by the Lunenburg Fire and Police Chiefs. An active securi-
  13|                          ty system shall be required for all RMD locations and approved by both the Lunenburg Fire and Police
  14|                          10 Chiefs and submitted to the Planning Board for final approval.
  15|                          (2) RMDs shall be open to inspection by the Fire Department, Police Department, Building Commis-
  16|                         sioner and the Board of Health with 24 hours' notice of request for such inspection to be made by the
  17|                          Town department or official. A property contact shall be available to such Town department or official
  18|                          24 hours a day, seven days a week.
  19|                          H. Documentation. The Planning Board shall be provided with all decisions or approvals, denials or
  20|                          other substantive actions by DPH regarding the RMD and all submittals of information relating to such
  21|                          activities between the applicant or RMD and DPH.
  22|                          § 250-4.18 15 Temporary moratorium on sale and distribution of recreational marijuana.
  23|                          Added 5-6-2017 ATM by Art. 33]
  24|                          A. Purpose.
  25|                          (1) By vote at the state election on November 8, 2016, the voters of the commonwealth approved a law
  26|                          regulating the cultivation, distribution, possession and use of marijuana for recreational purposes. The
  27|                         law provides that it is effective on December 15, 2016, and the Cannabis Control Commission is cur-
  28|                          rently required to issue regulations regarding implementation by March 15, 2018 (see Section 11 of
  29|                          Chapter 351 of the Acts of 2016).
  30|                          (2) Currently under the Zoning Bylaw, recreational marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers
  31|                          are not a permitted use in the Town, and any regulations promulgated by the State Cannabis Control
  32|                          Commission are expected to provide guidance to the Town in regulating recreational marijuana estab-
  33|                          lishments and marijuana retailers.
  34|                          (3) The regulation of recreational marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers raises novel and
  35|                          complex legal, planning, and public safety issues and the Town needs time to study and consider the
  36|                          regulation of recreational marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers and address such novel and
  37|                          complex issues, as well as to address the potential impact of the state regulations on local zoning and to
  38|                          undertake a planning process to consider amending the Zoning Bylaw regarding regulation of recrea-
  39|                          tional marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers and other uses related to the regulation of recre-
  40|                          ational marijuana. The Town intends to adopt a temporary moratorium on the use of land and structures
  41|                          in the Town for recreational marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers so as to allow the Town
  42|                          sufficient time to engage in a planning process to address effects of such structures and uses in the
  43|                          Town and to adopt provisions of the Zoning Bylaw in a manner consistent with sound land use plan-
  44|                          ning goals and objectives.
  45|                          B. Definitions.
  46|                          MANUFACTURE
  47|                          To compound, blend, extract, infuse or otherwise make or prepare a marijuana product.
  48|                          MARIJUANA ACCESSORIES
  49|                          Equipment, products, devices or materials of any kind that are intended or designed for use in planting,
  50|                          propagating, cultivating, growing, harvesting, manufacturing, compounding, converting, producing,
  51|                          processing, preparing, testing, analyzıng, packaging, repackaging, storing, containing, ingesting, inhal-
  52|                          ing or otherwise introducing marijuana into the human body.
  53|                                                                                              217

===PAGE 218=== (ocr, 49 lines)
   1|                          MARIJUANA CULTIVATOR
   2|                          An entity licensed to cultivate, process and package marijuana, to deliver marijuana to marijuana es-
   3|                          tablishments and to transfer marijuana to other marijuana establishments, but not to consumers.
   4|                          MARIJUANA ESTABLISHMENT
   5|                          A marijuana cultivator, marijuana testing facility, marijuana product manufacturer, marijuana retailer
   6|                          or any other type of licensed marijuana-related business.
   7|                          MARIJUANA PRODUCT MANUFACTURER
   8|                          An entity licensed to obtain, manufacture, process and package marijuana and marijuana products, to
   9|                          deliver marijuana and marijuana products to marijuana establishments and to transfer marijuana and
  10|                          marijuana products to other marijuana establishments, but not to consumers.
  11|                          MARIJUANA PRODUCTS
  12|                          Products that have been manufactured and contain marijuana or an extract from marijuana, including
  13|                          concentrated forms of marijuana and products composed of marijuana and other ingredients that are
  14|                         intended for use or consumption, including edible products, beverages, topical products, ointments,
  15|                          oils and tinctures.
  16|                         MARIJUANA TESTING FACILITY
  17|                          An entity licensed to test marijuana and marijuana products, including certification for potency and the
  18|                          presence of contaminants.
  19|                          MARIJUANA RETAILER
  20|                          An entity licensed to purchase and deliver marjuana and marjuana products trom marjuana establish-
  21|                          ments and to deliver, sell or otherwise transfer marijuana and marijuana products to marijuana estab-
  22|                          lishments and to consumers.
  23|                          C. Temporary moratorium. For the reasons set forth above and notwithstanding any other provision of
  24|                          the Zoning Bylaw to the contrary, the Town hereby adopts a temporary moratorium on the use of land
  25|                          or structures for recreational marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers. The moratorium shall
  26|                          be in effect through November 30, 2018. During the moratorium period, the Town shall undertake a
  27|                          planning process to address the potential impacts of recreational marijuana in the Town, consider the
  28|                          Cannabis Control Commission regulations regarding recreational marijuana establishments and mari-
  29|                          juana retailers and related uses, determine whether the Town will prohibit on-site consumption at rec-
  30|                          reational marijuana establishments and marijuana retailers and shall consider adopting new provisions
  31|                          of the Zoning Bylaw to address the impact and operation of recreational marijuana establishments and
  32|                          marijuana retailers and related uses.
  33|                          D. Severability. The provisions of this bylaw are severable. If any provision, paragraph, sentence, or
  34|                          clause of this bylaw or the application thereof to any person, establishment, or circumstances shall be
  35|                          held invalid.

   1|                          Earned vacation time up to and including 80 hours must be used in the year granted. No unused portion of this allowance shall
   2|                         be carried forward into a subsequent vacation year, nor shall any monetary compensation be given for such unused portion.
   3|                          Earned vacation time in excess of 80 hours should be used in the year granted, and no portion of such excess shall be carried
   4|                          forward into a subsequent year. If departmental scheduling or other serious extenuating circumstances preclude the use of all
   5|                         such excess in the year granted, the employee may request to shall receive compensation equivalent to such unused portion in a
   6|                          lump sum payable on the last first payroll warrant in Julyne, in addition to their regular salary, or may be allowed to carry over
   7|                         such excess as the Town may elect in its sole discretion. Any employee asserting a serious extenuating circumstance must
   8|                         submit a written request to his/her direct supervisor and such request must be approved by the direct supervisor and the Town
   9|                         Manager before the employee shall be compensated for, or allowed to carry over, such excess; provided, however, that such
  10|                         payment must be approved by the Department Head and written authorization signed by the Town Manager in advance of such
  11|                         payment.
  12|                         The vacation year shall begin July 1. In the first year of employment, employees shall accrue one (1) day of vacation leave
  13|                         (prorated based on number of hours worked each week) per month of service completed to a maximum of 80 hours to be
  14|                         available for use by the employee on the following July 1st. Vacation leave accrued each fiscal year will be available for use on
  15|                         the following July 1st. Any change in the rate of accrual shall occur on the employee's anniversary date. When an employee's
  16|                         anniversary date for the completion of the 5th, 10th-20 years occurs after July 1st, the employee shall receive vacation leave for
  17|                          the remainder of the year on a pro-rated basis.
  18|                         SECTION 21. FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE
  19|                         The Town agrees to abide by the provisions of the 1993 Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA). All eligible employees are
  20|                         entitled to up to twelve (12) weeks of unpaid leave for certain family and medical reasons in a one (1) year period. Employees
  21|                         are eligible for FMLA if they have worked for the Town for at least one (1) year and at least for one thousand two hundred and
  22|                         fifty (1,250) hours over the previous twelve (12) months.
  23|                         Unpaid FMLA leave must be granted for any of the following reasons:
  24|                         • To care for the employee's child after birth, or placement for adoption or foster care
  25|                         • To care for the employee's spouse, son, daughter, or parent, who has a serious health condition
  26|                         • For a serious health condition that makes the employee unable to perform the employee's job
  27|                         In accordance with the past practice Town's policy, the Town allows, at the option of the employee requires, the use of paid leave
  28|                         time during the FMLA absence including accumulated Sick Leave, Vacation Leave, and Personal Leave. The Town requires all
  29|                         employees applying for an FMLA leave to notify their Department Head, in writing, thirty (30) days prior to the leave, if possible.
  30|                         SECTION 28. DEFINITIONS
  31|                         Hourly Employee shall mean any employee of the Town who by virtue of their classified position is compensated at an hourly
  32|                         rate for services rendered. Hourly employees are not eligible for benefits (i.e. vacation, sick time, insurance, etc.).

   4|                            (1)   In exercising the powers granted by Subsection B above, the Board of Appeals shall act in accordance with
   5|                                   the provisions of MGL c. 40A, §§ 9, 11, 14, 15 and 16.
   6|                                  Where action by the Board of Appeals is required under this bylaw, a written application therefor shall be submitted
   7|                                   by delivery or by registered mail (with return receipt requested) to the Clerk of the Board of Appeals or to suchother
   8|                                   person as the Board may have authorized to receive such applications. If submission is by delivery, the Clerk or other
   9|                                   authorized person shall give a written receipt therefor, indicating the date of such submission. The Board of Appeals
  10|                                   shall hold a public hearing with regard to any such application within 65 days of the filing.
  11|                            (a)    In the case of special permits under Subsection B(2), the Board of Appeals shall act thereon within 90 days ofthe
  12|                                   filing of the application.
  13|                            (b)   In the case of appeals or applications for variances under Subsection B(1) and (3), the Board of Appeals shalt
  14|                                   act within 75 days of the filing of the application.
  15|                            (4)    Should the Board of Appeals fail to act within the time limits specified above, the application shall be deemed
  16|                                   approved and the Building Commissioner shall, upon receipt of evidence of such submission and failure to act, issue
  17|                                   forthwith a permit for the proposed use, provided such use is otherwise in conformity with this bylaw.

  36|                                   ARTICLE 17. To see if the Town will vote to amend the Town Bylaws by adding a Bylaw for the reduction of
  37|                                   plastic bags, or take any other action relative thereto. (Citizen Petition) (Board of Selectmen recommends approval)
  38|                                   (Finance Committee voted no financial impact). VOTED to amend the Code of Lunenburg by adding a new Chapter 92,
  39|                                   entitled Reduction of Plastic Bags as follows:
  40|                                                                                              231

===PAGE 232=== (ocr, 44 lines)
   1|                           Section 1. Purpose and Intent
   2|                           The production and use of thin-film single-use plastic checkout bags have significant impacts on the
   3|                           environment, including, but not limited to: contributing to the potential death of marine animals through
   4|                          ingestion and entanglement; contributing to pollution of the land environment; creating a burden to solid
   5|                           waste collection-and recycling facilities; clogging storm drainage systems; and requiring the use of
   6|                           millions of barrels of crude oil nationally for their manufacture. The purpose of this bylaw is to eliminate
   7|                           the usage of thin-film single-use plastic bags by all retail and grocery stores in the Town of
   8|                           Lunenburg, by June 1, 2019.
   9|                           Section 2. Definitions
  10|                                                      2.1 Checkout bag: A carryout bag provided by a store to a consumer at the
  11|                                                             point of sale. Checkout bags shall not include bags, whether plastic or
  12|                                                             not, in which loose produce or products are placed by the consumer to
  13|                                                             deliver such items to the point of sale or checkout area of the store.
  14|                                                       2.2 Grocery Store: Aretail establishment where more than fifty percent (50%)
  15|                                                             of the gross floor area is devoted to the sale of food products for home
  16|                                                             preparation and consumption, which typically also offers home care and
  17|                                                             personal care products.
  18|                                                       2.3 Retail Store: An establishment that offers the sale and display of
  19|                                                             merchandise within a building.
  20|                                                       2.1 Reusable checkout bag: A bag, with handles, that is specifically
  21|                                                            designed for multiple use and is made of thick plastic, cloth, fabric or
  22|                                                            other durable materials.
  23|                                                       2.2 Thin-film single-use plastic bags: Typically with plastic handles, these
  24|                                                            are bags with a thickness of 2.5 mils or less and are intended for
  25|                                                            single-use transport of purchased products.
  26|                           Section 3. Use Regulations
  27|                                                       3.1 Thin-film single-use plastic bags shall not be distributed, used, or sold for
  28|                                                            checkout or other purposes at any retail or grocery store within the Town of
  29|                                                            Lunenburg.
  30|                                                       3.2 Customers are encouraged to bring their own reusable or biodegradable
  31|                                                            shopping bags to stores. Retail            or grocery stores are strongly
  32|                                                            encouraged to make reusable checkout bags available for sale to
  33|                                                             costumers at a reasonable price.
  34|                                                       3.3 Thin-filmed plastic bags used to contain dry cleaning, newpapers, produce,
  35|                                                            meat, bulk foods, wet items and other similar merchandise, typically without
  36|                                                            handles, are still permissible.
  37|                           Section 4. Enforcement Process
  38|                           Enforcement of this bylaw shall be the responsibility of the Town Manager or his/her
  39|                          incorporating the process into other town duties as appropriate. Any retail or grocery store
  40|                           distributing plastic grocery bags in violation of this bylaw shall be subject to a non-criminal
  41|                           disposition fine as specified in Appendix A of the Regulations for Enforcement of Town
  42|                           Bylaws under M.G.L
  43|                           Chapter 40, 21D and the Bylaw for Non-Criminal Disposition of Violations. Any such
  44|                                                                                              232

===PAGE 233=== (ocr, 9 lines)
   1|                             fines shall be paid to the Town of Lunenburg.
   2|                             And to amend Appendix A of the Non-Criminal Disposition Bylaw by adding the following:
